newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian Central Bank refinancing rate changes.
newsitem.headline: Russian Central Bank refinancing rate changes.

text.p: Changes in the Central Bank of Russia's refinancing and Lombard rates.

The Central Bank does not operate a refinancing facility charged at the refinancing rate. The refinancing rate is little more than a benchmark for interbank lending, but also serves as an effective cap on Treasury bill yields, economists said. The Central Bank will only cut the rate when it is sure that yields will stay below this level.
T-bill yields have only gone above the rate once, during the 1996 presidential election campaign.

Feb 10 42 vs 48 no change 33 vs 36 42 vs 48

NOTE - The Central Bank introduced auctions for Lombard credits in early 1996. At the first auction on April 4, the rate for seven-day funds was 60 percent, and at subsequent auctions ranged from 51 to 75 percent. The Central Bank replaced the auctions in summer 1996 with three fixed-rate Lombard facilities, initially running for seven, 14 and 29 days. The two longer maturities were changed to 8-14 days and 15-30 days on December 2, 1996. The shorter maturity was changed to 3-7 days on February 10, 1997. Date when rate on 29-day loans cut to 60 from 62 percent unclear.
